chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, and Muawiya ibn Ammar, and Hammad, from al-Halby, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with hastening the circumambulation (Tawaf) for the elderly man and the woman who fears menstruation, before going out to Mina.
ai.seo_question: When can the elderly and women perform Tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the elderly and women to perform Tawaf al-Qudum early to avoid the specific difficulty of menstruation interrupting their Hajj rituals. It reflects the practical flexibility of the Imams in balancing ritual precision with the physical realities of the pilgrim, ensuring that essential obligations are not missed due to natural biological processes or age-related frailty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, and Muawiya Bin Ammar, and Hammad, from Al Halby, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with hastening the Tawaaf, for the aged old man, and the woman who fears the menstruation, before the going out to Mina’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar and Hammad from al-Halabiy all have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Old people, and women who are afraid of experiencing Hayd (menses), can perform Tawaf before leaving for Mina’.’”
